topic: Aleph Alpha Kolibri: open weights with a 1M-token context window
title: Aleph Alpha Kolibri: 1M context in open weights
description: Working description; the package stage overwrites.
hook_candidates: Kolibri promises a million tokens. Its own card says don't.
A million tokens of context, forty-seven gigabytes of download.
A million tokens isn't the whole story.
You've got the headlines. Your RAM has the answer.
Seventy-eight billion parameters, three point five billion awake.
Germany just open-sourced a million-token model.
Ollama can't load this week's biggest model.
Check your RAM before the million finds you.
A million tokens, if your memory can host them.
narration_full: A million tokens of context, forty-seven gigabytes of download. That's Kolibri, a German model with open weights, files you run yourself. You've seen million-token headlines all week and asked if it fits your machine. Context is how much text it reads at once. Aleph Alpha itself says stay at two hundred sixty-two thousand tokens or below for complex work. The headline's own footnote. It's a mixture of experts: each word, a receptionist wakes the few specialists needed. All seventy-eight billion parameters sit in memory. The community file needs a patched llama.cpp, the local runner, modified by hand. Ollama and LM Studio just stare. One measured llama.cpp setup needed one hundred twenty-eight gigabytes of system RAM. Count yours before you trust the headline.
analogy: receptionist: a company of specialists with a receptionist who wakes only the few you need; re-picks for every word
